newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia govt speaker under threat - paper.
newsitem.headline: Australia govt speaker under threat - paper.

text.p: Australian government member Bob Halverson position as speaker of parliament's lower house, the House of Representatives, may be under threat, a newspaper reported on Tuesday.
The Canberra Times cited government sources as saying Prime Minister John Howard and several senior ministers were placing increasing pressure on Halverson for being too independent.
As speaker, Halverson presides over the running of the house.

"It is understood that the animosity between Mr Howard, several ministers and the speaker, Bob Halverson, essentially over his rulings on supplementary questions, has left some MPs wondering whether Mr Halverson will be able to chalk up a year in the job, due in April," the paper said.
Halverson dealt with 83 supplementary questions in the first 53 days of the Howard parliament, which was elected on March 2 last year.

Supplementaries are follow-up questions in question time, the main opportunity for the opposition to quiz ministers. The speaker has the discretion to allow a supplementary question if he feels the main question was not answered adequately.

"Treasurer Peter Costello was asked seven supplementaries between May and December and his annoyance, and that of Mr Howard and Government Leader Peter Reith when asked such questions, is plain," the paper said.
"Mr Costello is often observed almost sneering at Mr Halverson."
Ahead of his March, 1996, election win, Howard pledged to increase the independence of the speaker.
Howard's Liberal-National coalition had accused speakers under the former Labor administration of lacking in independence.
